history.summary: An ARCHITECTURAL MONUMENT, not an active temple. Two freestanding ornamental gateways (toranas) in Maru-Gurjara style, about 40 feet tall, built of red and yellow sandstone on the bank of Sharmistha Lake just north of Vadnagar's walled town. Richly carved with battle and hunting scenes, floral/geometric motifs, kirtimukhas and divine figures; carving style resembles the Rudra Mahalaya at Siddhpur and the Sun Temple at Modhera. They may have been erected to commemorate a war victory and possibly served as the entrance to a large temple complex of which no remains survive; a folk attribution to the 15th-century poet Narsinh Mehta ('Narsinh Mehta's Chauri') is refuted by 12th-century architectural dating. The eastern toran stayed relatively intact and became a symbol of Gujarat; the ruined western one was re-erected by the Archaeological Survey of India in 2007. It is a Monument of National Importance (N-GJ-156) protected by the ASI. CSV ERROR: the CSV 'state' column holds 'Vadnagar', which is the town; the real state is Gujarat (district Mehsana).

name: Kirti Toran Temple Complex
town_description: Vadnagar (ancient Anandapura) in Mehsana district is a continuously inhabited town over two thousand years old, recorded by the 7th-century Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang and now on UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list. It is the ancestral home of the Nagar Brahmin community, the birthplace of Narendra Modi, and preserves medieval monuments such as the Kirti Toran, the Hatkeshwar temple and Sharmistha Lake.
